bug_semantics: In glx/vndcmds.c, CommonMakeCurrent() obtains oldTag as a direct pointer into a client's cl->contextTags array through GlxLookupContextTag(). When all 16 initial tag slots are occupied, the nested CommonMakeNewCurrent() -> GlxAllocContextTag() path in glx/vndservermapping.c grows that array with realloc(), which can free and move the allocation. The vulnerable ordering then calls GlxFreeContextTag(oldTag) through the stale pointer and zeros fields in freed heap memory. An authenticated local X client can reach the write by creating 17 GLX contexts, filling the first 16 tags with MakeCurrent(oldContextTag=0), and switching to the seventeenth with a nonzero oldContextTag so allocation occurs while oldTag is retained.
flaw_origin: Commit 4781f2a5a8c2c2b000374e2d87982a6701d5a6b3 tried to preserve the old context tag when CommonMakeNewCurrent() fails. It removed GlxFreeContextTag() from CommonLoseCurrent() and moved that free to after CommonMakeNewCurrent() succeeds, but did not account for GlxAllocContextTag() reallocating the same array that owns oldTag. That focused ordering change first created the dangling-pointer write; it was not a move, refactor, merge, release commit, or squash aggregate.
ai_marker: absent — the exact commit object for 4781f2a5a8c2c2b000374e2d87982a6701d5a6b3 names human author Doğukan Korkmaztürk <dkorkmazturk@nvidia.com>, human committer Olivier Fourdan <fourdan@gmail.com>, and only the trailer Signed-off-by: Doğukan Korkmaztürk <dkorkmazturk@nvidia.com>; it contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other AI marker.
evidence: First-party X.Org security advisory forwarded by X.Org maintainer Peter Hutterer at https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/07/08/2 identifies CVE-2026-56000/ZDI-CAN-30561, describes the retained cl->contextTags pointer, realloc-triggering 17th MakeCurrent request, stale GlxFreeContextTag() write, and names fixed releases xorg-server-21.1.24 and xwayland-24.1.13. It also expressly says the report against 21.1.16 could not be reproduced, the flaw is present on main/discontinued master and Xwayland, and 21.1.x distributions that backported 4781f2a5a8c2c2b000374e2d87982a6701d5a6b3 are definitely affected.

The first-party fix is https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver/-/commit/2779affbdb4354e894f490e56f962527d6125043 and its merge request is https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver/-/merge_requests/2250. The direct one-parent commit changes glx/vndcmds.c by moving GlxFreeContextTag(oldTag) ahead of CommonMakeNewCurrent(), explicitly states Fixes: 4781f2a5a8c2, and adds the 17-context ASan reproducer in test/pyxtest/test_glx.py.

numactl-prefixed git log -L :CommonMakeCurrent:glx/vndcmds.c traces the dangerous ordering directly to 4781f2a5a8c2c2b000374e2d87982a6701d5a6b3 and its repair directly to 2779affbdb4354e894f490e56f962527d6125043; the earlier function-import commit 8753218beae641e5c5ac2c2ba598cfb99a893cf4 kept oldTag safe by clearing/freeing it before CommonMakeNewCurrent(). git log -S'GlxFreeContextTag(oldTag)' -- glx/vndcmds.c returns only 4781f2a5a8c2c2b000374e2d87982a6701d5a6b3, corroborating it as the smallest original source change that wrote the vulnerable statement/order.

The introducer patch changes only glx/vndcmds.c: it removes the successful free from CommonLoseCurrent(), retains oldTag across CommonMakeNewCurrent(), and adds GlxFreeContextTag(oldTag) afterward. At 4781f2a5a8c2c2b000374e2d87982a6701d5a6b3, glx/vndcmds.c:220 obtains oldTag, glx/vndcmds.c:181 reaches GlxAllocContextTag(), and glx/vndcmds.c:270 performs the stale free; glx/vndservermapping.c:91-140 contains the reallocating allocator and glx/vndservermapping.c:142-169 contains the lookup/free operations.

Direct-parent tree verification at 3852b0d10a061348ea8214fbcbef3c5c08cac0b6:glx/vndcmds.c shows CommonLoseCurrent() calling GlxFreeContextTag(tagInfo) on success and CommonMakeCurrent() immediately setting oldTag = NULL before any CommonMakeNewCurrent() call. Therefore the vulnerable retained-pointer/free-after-allocation sequence is absent in the immediate parent.

Version membership cross-check: 4781f2a5a8c2c2b000374e2d87982a6701d5a6b3 is contained in Xwayland tags beginning with xwayland-23.0.99.901 and released xwayland-23.1.0, through xwayland-24.1.12; xwayland-24.1.12:glx/vndcmds.c still frees oldTag after CommonMakeNewCurrent(). The fix backport 9ca6ab9dea4cc8bce8a0258318976c5c690386a3 is contained by xwayland-24.1.13, and that tag's glx/vndcmds.c frees/nulls oldTag before allocation. The original mainline fix 2779affbdb4354e894f490e56f962527d6125043 is contained by later development tags including xwayland-26.0.99.901.

The xorg-server-21.1 line requires the advisory's qualification rather than a blanket affected claim: xorg-server-21.1.23:glx/vndcmds.c has the safe parent-era ordering and the original BIC is not an ancestor of any 21.1 release tag. During the 21.1.24 security integration, d6fff22bc8b464dbadf3bc1fb858bd5a91c86849 cherry-picked the BIC and its immediate successor d6d96084f305a142eb3db7f720d7edd21e4c98b4 cherry-picked the fix; xorg-server-21.1.24 contains d6d96084f305a142eb3db7f720d7edd21e4c98b4. Thus the released 21.1.24 tree is fixed, while downstream 21.1.x trees that independently backported the BIC without the fix are affected, exactly as the first-party advisory states.

BIC-only attribution used numactl-prefixed git cat-file -p 4781f2a5a8c2c2b000374e2d87982a6701d5a6b3. Its single parent proves it is not a merge, its focused patch needs no squash decomposition, and its author, committer, message, and sole Signed-off-by trailer contain no AI marker. AI assistance on any later fix is outside the protocol's BIC-only attribution decision.
reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle is causally closed. The pre-4781f2a5a8c2 tree frees the old tag before allocating a replacement, so realloc cannot leave a later oldTag use. The focused one-parent commit 4781f2a5a8c2c2b000374e2d87982a6701d5a6b3 moved that free across CommonMakeNewCurrent() to address failed-switch semantics, thereby retaining a direct array-element pointer across a realloc-capable call and first creating the UAF write. Its direct parent was inspected and lacks that sequence, while -L and -S history exclude the earlier import and later fix as the origin. The flaw shipped in Xwayland from 23.1.0 through 24.1.12 and was repaired in 24.1.13 by backport 9ca6ab9dea4cc8bce8a0258318976c5c690386a3; mainline was repaired directly by 2779affbdb4354e894f490e56f962527d6125043. The 21.1 branch was safe unless the BIC was backported, and the 21.1.24 release contains both backported origin and immediate repair. Finally, the exact BIC commit object has no AI attribution marker, so later fix provenance cannot change the BIC-only result and the correct closed verdict is NOT_AI.
